title: Token bundling: weighted handoff micro-run (scratch notes)
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad: test a small "hybrid' token-bundling policy that hands off remaining tokens between priority lanes using a weight factor (w).
- Motivation: reduce P99 tail on mixed short/long request mixes without blowing up avg latency for short requests.

Experiment matrix (local GPU dev cluster, small fleet emulation):
- Model: rwv2-small quant (8-bit), seq len 512
- Worker config: 4 replicas, allow 2 concurrent requests per worker
- Arrival mix: 70% short (10-30 tokens), 30% long (200-400 tokens)
- QPS: steady 120 qps; injected microbursts of +60 qps for 30s every 5 minutes (to simulate client spikes)
- Policies compared:
  * baseline: strict per-priority lane batching (no handoff)
  * naive-handoff: unconditional handoff of leftover tokens to low-priority lane when high queue > 100ms
  * weighted-handoff(w): handoff fractional workload proportional to w*(high_queue_depth)/(total_queue_depth) — tested w in {0.2, 0.5, 1.0}

Commands used (local runner):
- runner --profile mixed --qps 120 --burst 60:30 --clients 400 --policy baseline --out run_baseline.json
- runner --profile mixed --qps 120 --burst 60:30 --clients 400 --policy weighted-handoff --w 0.5 --out run_w05.json

Quick aggregated observations (from telemetry sampler, 5% sampling, 3 runs each):
- Baseline:
  p50: 23ms, p95: 127ms, p99: 410ms, max: 980ms, tokens/s per GPU: 52k
- Naive-handoff:
  p50: 27ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 360ms, max: 720ms, tokens/s per GPU: 48k
- Weighted-handoff w=0.2:
  p50: 24ms, p95: 130ms, p99: 330ms, max: 650ms, tokens/s per GPU: 50k
- Weighted-handoff w=0.5:
  p50: 26ms, p95: 125ms, p99: 285ms, max: 540ms, tokens/s per GPU: 49k
- Weighted-handoff w=1.0:
  p50: 30ms, p95: 160ms, p99: 320ms, max: 600ms, tokens/s per GPU: 46k

Interpretation / rough notes:
- Weighted handoff with w=0.5 gave the best P99 reductions for mixed traffic while keeping p95 comparable.
- w too low (0.2) reduces tokens throughput less effectively; w too high (1.0) starts to hurt short-request p50 and overall token throughput (more context-switching / larger batches delaying short items).
- Naive unconditional handoff reduces p99 somewhat but increases p50 and drops tokens/s noticeably — suggests contention introduced by blind handoffs.

Telemetry traces looked like: (very rough ascii visualization of p99 window over time)
- baseline: ___/^^^^^^^\n- w=0.5: ___/^^^--^^\n- naive: ___/^^^^--^^^^

Edge cases noticed:
- During the 30s microburst ramp, if long-request fraction briefly jumps above 45%, weighted-handoff policies suffer an oscillation where long lane consumes almost all slots then releases; saw a small hop in p99 for short requests for ~10s.
- KV-cache hit rates matter: when cache hit drops below 65% (simulated by cold runs), the benefits of handoff are amplified (because long requests pay higher CPU/token cost and bundling them efficiently matters more).

Quick conclusions (draft):
- Weighted handoff (w around 0.4-0.6) is a promising heuristic for mixed workloads where short-request latency matters.
- Need to test at larger scale (>= 32 GPUs) and with more realistic client mixes (real RLHF-style long tails) before listing as recommended policy.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- Run cluster-scale test on staging (scale tester ticket) -> try QPS patterns: 300 steady + 100 bursts, 10k clients. (assign to @Ravi)
- Add a smoothing term to weight calculation to prevent oscillation when long fraction rapidly changes (experiment: momentum factor m in [0.2,0.6]).
- Instrument to capture short-request starvation metric (percentage of short requests whose latency increased > 2x during burst).
- Write short PR to add weighted-handoff option in policy config + unit tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (draft).

Notes to self:
- Keep results rough in drive; will formalize graph exports if staging run looks good.
- When writing PR description highlight: cost-neutral (no hardware change), small perf win for tail, tunable knob, graceful fallback to baseline.

Related links / quick references:
- Experiment runner: /home/jasm/bench/runners/dev-mix-runner.sh
- Sampling dashboard (local): http://localhost:18080/telemetry/last-run (remember to reset sampler before next run)

End of scratchpad.
